summary: Steve Grothoff continues the Galatians series in 4:8-20, where Paul's tone turns from stern argument to a pastor's plea. Having come to know God, or rather to be known by him, the Galatians were drifting back to the worthless principles they once served, and Paul feared his labor was in vain. Idolatry is anything placed above God, and Paul lives out the freedom he preaches instead of imposing rules. Teachers who courted followers for themselves led the church astray, but Paul only wanted them to follow Christ well, like a parent in labor until Christ is formed in them.
takeaways: God knows us and loves us, so returning to old habits that never satisfied us makes no sense.
Idolatry is putting anything above God, whether social media, sports, jobs, possessions, family, or even knowledge about God.
Paul practices what he preaches and becomes all things to all people for the sake of the gospel, without changing the message.
Leaders should want people to follow Christ well, not to gather followers for themselves; devotion matters more than numbers.
As a church we hold the whole truth of Scripture without compromise, stay unified in it, and receive God's word as Christ's message rather than critique the preacher.
